correctness.rationale: For each ternary five-word x, D1(x) is the SET of its distinct length-four subsequences by one deletion. The explicit 24 codewords have pairwise disjoint D1 shadows, giving lower bound 24. The pinned verify.py gives 81 positive integer weights c_z with sum 348, scale 14; independently reconstructed all 243 input deletion shadows and checked min_x sum_{z in D1(x)}c_z =14, and verified disjointness of the 24 source witnesses (using 78 distinct output words). Any code then satisfies 14|C|≤348; integer |C|≤24. Finite enumeration exhausts the exact 3^5 domain, not a partial sample. This establishes N(5,3,1)=24.

evidence: General fractional matching upper bound in arXiv:1211.3128 gives rounded 24, but its lower bound is 17. Li–Houghten Table IV max T_{βγ}(5) size17.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A general upper bound of 24 alone does not imply equality; full published Tenengolts family size 17 is strictly smaller. The new 24-word witness closes the gap.

value.rationale: Exact natural ternary length-5 one-deletion optimum closes a specific documented seven-codeword construction gap (17 to 24) against the existing rounded fractional upper bound. The constructive primal witness plus independently checkable exact dual is useful as a small synchronization-code benchmark, even without a general family or census.

limitations: The exact result is only n=5, alphabet 3, one deletion; no classification of all extremal codes or asymptotics claimed.
